A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same EPG research work, with 22 pages covering Sections 1–6 and Appendices A–F. Text and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, tables, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original ImageNet diffusion and consistency experiments, efficiency measurements, ablations, representation analyses, and generated samples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including the EPG results in Tables 1–6 and the ablations and qualitative analyses in Appendices C–F.

M1.justification: The encoder pre-training objectives, temperature schedule, encoder–decoder architecture, diffusion fine-tuning, and consistency-model auxiliary loss are unchanged. The preconditioning notation edit does not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1K for the same diffusion and consistency-generation tasks, retaining ImageNet-256/512 benchmarks, ImageNet-224 ablations, and the same noisy-input analyses.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–6 and the appendix analyses. PixelFlow’s citation changes from Chen et al. (2025) to Chen et al. (2025c), but the comparator and its results remain identical. Added references introduce no evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, preprocessing, metrics, sample counts, and sampling procedures are retained. Table 9 replaces t_n with t in consistency-training preconditioning, aligning notation with the continuous-time protocol already specified in v2.

E4.justification: The scalability, auxiliary-loss, temperature, pre-training-loss, and encoder-flexibility studies are unchanged, including Figure 3 and Tables 12–13. Appendices D–F retain the same convergence, feature, noisy-representation, and qualitative analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version adds or revises repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures. Benchmark reporting remains based on the same point estimates.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative examples are retained. Tables 1, 2, and 4 still report diffusion FIDs of 1.58 on ImageNet-256 and 2.35 on ImageNet-512, and one-step consistency FID of 8.82, under the same respective settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–10 are unchanged, with no added assumptions, proofs, or derivations. Table 9’s t_n-to-t edit is a notation correction consistent with the previously stated continuous-time setting.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about two-stage pixel-space training, generation quality, efficiency, scalability, and high-resolution consistency training without pre-trained VAEs or diffusion models.

C2.justification: Interpretations of semantic consistency, encoder adaptation, and scaling are unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitation concerning performance behind REPA/RAE and the same explanation attributing this gap to training compute.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 explicitly identifies EDM as the source of the already documented input preconditioning, while Table 9 clarifies its continuous-time notation. This is a limited documentation refinement; hyperparameters, hardware, timings, preprocessing, and code-access information are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: Four bibliography entries are added: Caron et al. (2021), Li et al. (2024), and Chen et al. (2025a, 2025b) on preference mode collapse and S2-guidance. These additions do not substantively expand Section 5 or revise the paper’s research positioning.

P1.justification: The publication notice replaces 'Preprint', the author footnote changes from 'Project Lead' to 'Corresponding Author', and there are limited wording, notation, and reference-metadata edits. The section organization and substantive prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The title wraps differently, references reflow across pages 11–13, and final-page figure spacing shifts slightly. A white-text line of raw citation keys appears after Figure 18. All 18 figures and 13 tables are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 provides a small preconditioning clarification and bibliography updates while preserving the scientific argument, evidence, and limitations. The added references receive no substantive discussion, and the final page gains white-text citation keys. These limited editorial benefits and defects do not produce a meaningful net change in overall quality.
